source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #357 (branch fix/320-resource-validation at head 8a0e41d3639ccce08d2e352dc7cb9e2a1fd83cd4 — the Codex P2 round-2 fix on top of the Codex P2 fix and the #320 change: the export (sub resource) ascription check accepts abstract resource faces (a sub resource-bounded generic, possibly behind an eq alias), so a named sub-ascribed export can itself be re-exported with a further (sub resource) ascription; the tree also contains the #320 change merged with current main b20ed79513bbb12f6e4447158fd4028808ac129b (PR #353); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45613949341, 45613966977 and 45613982565 against the branch and pull-request run 45612656036, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #357 (Codex P2 round-2 fix: accept abstract resource faces in the export (sub resource) ascription check). The fix commit 8a0e41d sits on top of the tree re-baselined for the Codex P2 fix in 0c16fdc; its CI run tripped the gate on twelve series. Attribution was isolated two ways. Against the previous branch head’s checked-in baseline (the tree of 0c16fdc), the delta is confined to the stripped file and stripped .text of the three configurations that link telomere-component, in both profiles: in release, stripped file +600 B (component), +616 B (wasi) and +600 B (wasi-threads) and stripped .text +496 B in each; in release-size, stripped file +496 B / +512 B / +512 B and stripped .text +416 B / +432 B / +432 B; every other series is byte-identical. Against unmodified main (workflow_dispatch runs 45598772332, 45598789232 and 45598803018 on main at b20ed79513bbb12f6e4447158fd4028808ac129b, unchanged since those runs), the delta remains confined to the component-linking configurations recorded for #320 and the two Codex fixes. All twelve series exceed the checked-in baseline, so those twelve are re-baselined to the branch measurements. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the four branch samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is now the release component stripped file series at +11.16% (2,433,656 B to 2,705,288 B); the release core-nosimd stripped file series is unchanged at +9.83% (1,275,448 B to 1,400,840 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
